title: Duchy of Racibórz
capsule: The Duchy of Racibórz was a Piast principality in Upper Silesia centred on Racibórz (German: Ratibor), created in 1172 for Mieszko I Tanglefoot following the partition of the Duchy of Silesia; Mieszko absorbed the neighboring Duchy of Opole in 1202, temporarily merging the two territories. Duke Leszek swore homage to John of Bohemia in 1327, bringing Racibórz into the Bohemian orbit; his death without heirs in 1336 ended the local Piast line, and King John enfeoffed Nicolas II of Opava with the duchy. Control passed through the Přemyslid dukes of Opava until the duchy merged with Opole under Jan II the Good in 1521 and fell to the Habsburgs in 1532.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory around Racibórz is well established from medieval Silesian charters; precise boundary shifts with Opole during 13th–14th century reorganizations are known only in outline.
